### context: full
SHEET METAL COST INPUT RULES:
  Lines marked deterministic are computed from the measured geometry and will REPLACE whatever you return for them — restate them, do not re-derive them.
  Lines marked UNDECIDED are yours to answer: nothing in the geometry settles them. Answer from the drawing, the photo or the part name, and say which you used.
  thicknessMm=12.25  [raised from 2.40 mm (bulk wall 2·V/S over 4 bend face(s)) to the mass-consistent floor — measured 1037 cm³ over a 336×252 blank needs ≥12.25 mm; a thinner read means the blank could not weigh as much as the part — deterministic, use verbatim]
  blankLengthMm=336  [ESTIMATED from the formed part’s bounding box × 1.05 — no developed blank was supplied. A formed part’s footprint is not its flat pattern, so this can be well out in either direction; upload the FASTBLANK DXF to replace it with the real profile — deterministic, use verbatim]
  blankWidthMm=252  [ESTIMATED from the formed part’s bounding box × 1.05 — no developed blank was supplied. A formed part’s footprint is not its flat pattern, so this can be well out in either direction; upload the FASTBLANK DXF to replace it with the real profile — deterministic, use verbatim]
  perimeterMm=1176  [2 × (336 + 252) of the blank rectangle — ignores the outline shape and every hole, so the blanking force is understated; upload the FASTBLANK DXF for the real cut length — deterministic, use verbatim]
  pressId=press-400t  [cut 1176 mm × 12.25 mm × 170 MPa ÷ 9,807 N/t = 250 t + bending 0.166 (1.33 ÷ an 8t die opening) × 640 mm × 12.25 mm × 213 MPa UTS (170 MPa shear ÷ 0.8, engineering-typical) ÷ 9,807 N/t = 28 t, + 10% stripper (engineering-typical) = 306 t, × 1.25 safety; die 1844 mm long (4 station(s) × 361 mm pitch + 400 mm (engineering-typical)) — the smallest press over 383 t with a bolster that takes it (press-400t: 2500 mm, typical) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  numOps=4  [pierce + 2 forming station(s) for 4 bend(s) at ~3 a station + cut-off = 4 — deterministic, use verbatim]
  pressLine=coil-fed  [bent part: run from coil through one die, no addendum — deterministic, use verbatim]
  pressesInLine=1  [one press, coil-fed — deterministic, use verbatim]
  blankingMethod=none  [coil-fed die — the blank is cut in the die — deterministic, use verbatim]
  blanksPerMin=0  [none — the blank is cut in the die — deterministic, use verbatim]
  drawAddendumMm=0  [bent part: run from coil through one die, no addendum — deterministic, use verbatim]
  pitchMm=361  [blank 336 mm + 25 mm web (max(3, 2 × gauge)) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  stripWidthMm=301  [blank 252 mm + 2 × 25 mm edge margin — deterministic, use verbatim]
  strokesPerMin=32  [min(feed 18,000 mm/min ÷ 361 mm pitch = 50, press-400t max 40 SPM, typical) × 0.8 for 4 bends (one step at ≥ 4, ≥ 8, ≥ 14) = 32.0 → 32 SPM — feed rate and de-rate engineering-typical, not sourced — deterministic, use verbatim]
  dieCostGBP=66555  [progressive die, 4 station(s), 847 cm² blank, 170 MPa shear: £66,555 — toolmaker build-up of the die: Strip layout & die design 109.6 h × £58.42/h £6,400 + Die set (plates, guides, bolster) £5,610 + Die-set machining & fitting 41.9 h × £52.37/h £2,196 + Punch + die tool steel × 4 station(s) £2,576 + Wire-EDM cutting edges × 4 228.4 h × £58.42/h £13,343 + Station CNC machining × 4 293.7 h × £52.37/h £15,378 + Bench fitting & try-in × 4 130.5 h × £48.35/h £6,310 + Die tryout — 4 strip runs 32 h × £85.61/h £2,740 + Toolmaker overhead + profit £12,002 = £66,555 (CostVision engineering heuristic; toolroom £/h from the active book); the kernel's face-count parametric (UK basis, not country-adjusted) said £92,300 (not used) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  dieLife=1050000  [170 MPa shear at 12.25 mm on a progressive die: 1,000,000 × (300 ÷ 170 MPa)^1.3 × 0.500 (1.5 ÷ 12.25 mm gauge, ≥ 0.5), 50k–3M, to the nearest 10k = 1,050,000 hits (CostVision engineering heuristic, not sourced) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  dieType=progressive  [coil-fed progressive die, 4 stations — deterministic, use verbatim]
  process=Progressive stamping (4 stations)  [high volume (100,000/yr): stamping — laser + brake is not an option: 12.25 mm is beyond a fibre laser's economic range — deterministic, use verbatim]
  materialId=mat-aa5754-sheet  [aluminium → mat-aa5754-sheet (representative coil grade — not a drawing callout) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  netWeightKg=2.8  [1037 cm³ × 0.0027 kg/cm³ (aluminium, confirmed by engineer) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  shearStrengthMPa=170  [170 MPa — engineering-typical for a 5xxx / 6xxx aluminium sheet — not the grade’s own — deterministic, use verbatim]
  route=stamping  [stamping — laser + brake is not an option: 12.25 mm is beyond a fibre laser's economic range — deterministic, use verbatim]
  manning=0.5  [coil-fed press-400t: one operator tends two automatic presses (engineering-typical) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  rejectRate=0.015  [press-shop scrap (start-up, coil ends, splits), engineering-typical 1–2% — deterministic, use verbatim]
  setupHoursPerChange=1  [1 h to change a coil-fed die on a press-400t (engineering-typical) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  batchSize=5000  [100,000/yr ÷ 20 runs a year, 50–5,000 — the shop's standard batch — deterministic, use verbatim]
  dieMaintenanceFraction=0.05  [die maintenance (sharpening, springs, inserts) 5% of the die a year — engineering-typical 5–10%, charged for every year of the amortisation — deterministic, use verbatim]
  finish question: UNDECIDED — needs "Is the part coated or surface-treated?" (None — bare part | Powder coat (iron phosphate pre-treat) | E-coat / KTL (zirconium pre-treat) | Sulphuric anodise (aluminium))
  finishRoute=  [not asked yet — costed bare (answer "Is the part coated?" to price a finish) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  finishAreaM2=0.122  [measured surface 1220.0 cm² = 0.1220 m² — the whole wetted surface; a masked or machined-after-coating face is in it — deterministic, use verbatim]
